title: HTTP in and out: platform-http, REST DSL, to and toD
summary: Three ways to expose HTTP, how path parameters arrive, why 405 differs from 404, and when an endpoint must be dynamic.

steps.title: Three ways to expose HTTP
body: 1. **platform-http**: one route per path, on the web server the runtime already has (like Kestrel).
`from: platform-http:/books/{isbn}?httpMethodRestrict=GET`. Simplest; ideal for learning.
2. **REST DSL**: one definition lists several verbs and paths, each forwarding to a `direct:` route. Like a
controller with several actions.
```yaml
- rest:
path: /books
get:
- path: /{isbn}
to: direct:getBook
post:
- to: direct:createBook
3. **Contract-first REST DSL**: the REST definition is generated from an OpenAPI file, and each operation goes to
`direct:<operationId>`. Best for real APIs with several operations (module 4).
In all three, a path parameter `{isbn}` arrives as a **header** called `isbn`.
`httpMethodRestrict=GET` makes other verbs answer **405 Method Not Allowed**, like `MapGet` versus `Map`.

items: A quick learning spike with one endpoint
Five operations on `/orders`, no contract yet
A partner API whose OpenAPI contract was agreed first

steps.prompt: Complete the REST definition: `GET /books/{isbn}` goes to `direct:getBook`.
steps.explain: REST DSL paths use `{name}` templates, and `to` must name an endpoint URI, here an in-process `direct:` route.

steps.title: to versus toD
body: Calling a backend is a **producer** step:
- **`to`**: a **fixed** URI, resolved once when the route starts and reused. `{{placeholders}}` are fine,
because they are filled at startup.
- **`toD`** (*to dynamic*): the URI is evaluated **for every message**, so it can contain Simple:
`toD: http:catalogue:8080/api/books/${variable.isbn}`. In Karavan this is the **Dynamic** switch.
```yaml
- to:  "http:catalogue:8080/api/health"               # same every time
- toD: "http:catalogue:8080/api/books/${variable.isbn}" # different per message
The price of `toD`: Camel creates and caches one endpoint per distinct URI (the cache is bounded,
`cacheSize`). Fine for ids; for millions of distinct values, keep the URI fixed and pass the variable
part as a header or query option instead.

options: The `${...}` is not evaluated per message, so every call uses the literal text and fails or hits the wrong URL; use `toD`
Camel evaluates it anyway; `to` and `toD` are aliases
Camel refuses to start because `to` cannot contain `/`
steps.explain: Only `toD` evaluates the URI per exchange. This is one of the first mistakes everyone makes.
That is the endpoint cache `toD` keeps: one endpoint per distinct resolved URI.

steps.prompt: `from: platform-http:/books/{isbn}?httpMethodRestrict=GET`. A client sends `DELETE /books/123`. What does it get?
steps.explain: The path exists but the verb is not allowed: 405. A 404 means no route matches the path at all. Getting this right tells clients whether to fix the URL or the method.

steps.title: Match a path template
prompt: Write `Dictionary<string, string>? Match(string template, string path)`:
- split both on `/` (ignore empty segments, so leading and trailing slashes don't matter);
- a template segment `{name}` matches any non-empty segment and captures it, URL-decoded (`Uri.UnescapeDataString`);
- other segments must be equal, ignoring case;
- return the captured values (an empty dictionary when there are none), or `null` if it does not match.
starter: Dictionary<string, string>? Match(string template, string path)
solution: Dictionary<string, string>? Match(string template, string path)

steps.title: 404 or 405?
prompt: The tests declare `record RouteDef(string Method, string Template, string Id);` and give you `Match` from the previous step (already in your editor below; keep it).
Write `(int Status, string? RouteId, Dictionary<string, string>? Params) Dispatch(List<RouteDef> routes, string method, string path)`:
- the first route whose template matches **and** whose method equals `method` (ignore case) → `(200, its Id, the params)`;
- otherwise, if some template matched but no method did → `(405, null, null)`;

if (string.Equals(r.Method, method, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) return (200, r.Id, values);
return pathMatched ? (405, null, null) : (404, null, null);

Only return 405 after looking at every route: a later route may allow the method.
